defects.description: Step 8 puts 'the rotate response payload' into the audit event metadata. That payload contains the new key's plaintext, so the secret is persisted in audit_events, violating R6 (secrets never in audit events or logs) and AC6.

The rotate body uses grace_hours (default 24, max 168) instead of the spec's grace_seconds (default 86400, allowed 0 to 604800). Name and unit drift: AC1 (3600 seconds) and AC4 (604801 returns 400) cannot be expressed, and the planned test uses grace_hours: 169 instead.
defects.location: plan.md step 1; plan.md Test strategy; spec.md R1, AC1, AC4

defects.description: New key material is generated ad hoc (32-byte hex secret, bcrypt cost 10, prefix taken from the first 8 chars of the secret) instead of with apikey.Generate. Verifier.Verify expects the lk_<prefix>_<secret> format and a sha256 hash, so rotated keys never authenticate; this breaks the NFR 'existing key format and hashing', and a prefix cut from the secret leaks secret bytes.

Revoke only evicts the key from the verifier cache of the instance that served the revoke. The other API instances (12 per the spec) keep returning the cached key until the cache entry expires, and cmd/server/main.go builds the verifier with KEY_CACHE_TTL defaulting to 10 minutes, so R4/AC2 (rejected on every instance within 5 s) fails. Grace-expired old keys lag the same way because cache hits are returned without re-checking Active. The AC2 test only checks the same verifier.
defects.location: plan.md steps 6-7; plan.md Test strategy; fixture/cmd/server/main.go; fixture/internal/apikey/apikey.go

defects.description: Step 7 exports the verifier's internal cache as Verifier.Cache with a Delete(hash) method and gives KeysAPI a *apikey.Verifier field so the HTTP handler reaches into auth hot-path internals, breaking the apikey package's encapsulation (Verifier's cache is deliberately unexported).

Audit events are written with a hand-written INSERT into audit_events via a type assertion a.Store.(store.Execer), bypassing the audit package and the KeysAPI.Audit writer that Create already uses (audit.Event / audit.Writer), duplicating insertSQL in the handler layer.

Audit insert failures are logged and the request still succeeds, and the audit write happens after the change commits. This contradicts R5/AC3: if the audit write fails the operation must fail (500) and nothing changes (no new key, no expiry).

The test strategy has no test for AC3 (audit insert fails, rotate returns 500 and no new key exists) or AC6 (no audit event contains the plaintext), and the AC1 test does not first assert both keys authenticate or use the 3600/3601 s boundary.
defects.location: plan.md Test strategy; spec.md AC1, AC3, AC6

tensions.description: Risk sees that local eviction cannot reach the other instances, whose verifiers keep keys for the 10-minute KEY_CACHE_TTL set in cmd/server/main.go, and naturally recommends re-checking revocation/expiry in the database on every request (or bypassing the cache). Architecture objects to exporting the cache and recommends an encapsulated Verifier.Invalidate/Forget method, which keeps the cache but is still local-only. Risk's fix breaks the NFR (no per-request DB round trip, p99 under 2 ms at about 20k rps); architecture's fix leaves revocation broken on 11 of 12 instances. The staleness bound lives in main.go's env default, not in apikey.go, the module architecture is reasoning about.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Bypass or remove the verifier cache so every request checks revoked_at/expires_at in the database.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Keep the cache unexported; replace step 7 with an encapsulated Verifier.Invalidate method called by Revoke.
tensions.reconciliation: Keep the cache and keep it encapsulated (drop step 7; at most a Verifier.Invalidate for same-instance immediacy), and bound staleness on every instance by setting KEY_CACHE_TTL to 5s or less where cmd/server/main.go builds the verifier (risk-side fact: the TTL is that env default, not fixed in apikey). With NewVerifier's TTL argument (architecture-side fact: the cache is the mechanism that keeps verification off the database) each instance re-reads a key at most once per 5 s, meeting R4 for revoked and grace-expired keys with no pub/sub and no per-request DB call. Test AC2 with two Verifiers sharing one store and clock.Fixed advanced 5 s.

tensions.description: Architecture wants the raw INSERT replaced by the audit writer KeysAPI already has, a.Audit.Write, exactly as Create uses it. Consistency wants an audit failure to fail the request and leave nothing changed. In production a.Audit is wired in cmd/server/main.go as audit.NewQueue(audit.NewSQL(st), 4096), whose Write enqueues and always returns nil, outside any transaction. Following architecture's fix makes consistency's R5/AC3 guarantee impossible: failures are never seen and the key change commits regardless. The hazard is in the caller's wiring, not in audit.go.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Write audit events through KeysAPI.Audit (audit.Writer) as Create does, instead of a hand-written INSERT.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Make an audit write failure return 500 and roll back the rotate/revoke change.
tensions.reconciliation: Use the audit package but not the injected queued writer: inside the same Store.WithTx as CreateKey/SetExpiry (or Revoke), call audit.NewSQL(ex).Write(ctx, ev) with the transaction's Execer and return its error, so a failed insert rolls back the new key and the expiry (AC3). Needs the architecture-side fact that audit.SQL accepts any Execer and WithTx exposes one, and the consistency-side fact that R5 requires synchronous, atomic failure, which rules out a.Audit (the Queue wired in main.go). Leave a.Audit for best-effort events such as key.created, keep plaintext out of metadata.

tensions.description: Tests wants an AC3 test in keys_test.go with the existing fakeStore the plan reuses: make the audit Exec fail, assert 500 and that no new key exists. Consistency wants the audit write moved into the rotate transaction so its failure rolls back CreateKey and SetExpiry. The fakeStore's WithTx just calls fn(f, f) and CreateKey writes straight into the map, so there is no rollback: against the consistency-correct implementation (CreateKey, SetExpiry, then audit in the tx) the tests lens's AC3 test fails, and making it pass would push the handler to audit before writing or to skip work, distorting the implementation. The rollback the requirement depends on exists only in store.PG.WithTx (pgx.BeginFunc).
tensions.lens_a_fix: Add a keys_test.go case that injects an audit Exec error into fakeStore and asserts a 500 and an unchanged key set.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Do the audit insert inside Store.WithTx after CreateKey/SetExpiry and return its error so the transaction rolls back.
tensions.reconciliation: Keep the in-transaction ordering and make the test double honour transactions: give fakeStore an execErr knob and a WithTx that runs fn against a staged copy of the key map and commits it only when fn returns nil, mirroring PG.WithTx's BeginFunc commit/rollback. Then the AC3 test asserts 500, no new key, and the old key without expires_at. Needs the tests-side fact (fakeStore.WithTx has no rollback) and the consistency-side fact (R5's 'nothing changes' is delivered by transaction rollback, not by ordering).
